neighbours.label: relative pronoun 'that'/'who' opening a restrictive relative clause right after a noun, not complementizer or demonstrative 'that'
fire: My aunt kept every postcard that her sister mailed from Spain.
We hired two carpenters who had rebuilt the old mill.
The museum displays a sword that a farmer found in his field.
Last week I finally read the novel that my teacher recommended.
In the end, the students who finished early helped the others.
Our town still uses a bridge that the Romans built.
She called the plumber who fixed our sink last spring.
He donated the bicycle that his son had outgrown.
quiet: My aunt told me that her sister mailed postcards from Spain.
We heard that two carpenters had rebuilt the old mill.
The museum announced that a farmer found a sword in his field.
Last week I finally realized that my teacher was right.
In the end, everyone agreed that the students worked hard.
Our town still uses that bridge near the old market.
She claimed that the plumber fixed our sink last spring.
He knew that his son had outgrown the bicycle.

predictions: relative that/who after a noun fires; complementizer 'that' after a verb and demonstrative 'that' stay quiet
